# 6502DOS API

<!-- Generated by tools/genapi.py from tools/api.py. Do not edit. -->

Version 0.1.0.

Conventions:

- A program makes a call with JSR to its entry in RAM: GATE_ENTRIES + 3 * the call number. The Entry column gives it; api.inc names it API_NAME.
- Arguments go in A, X, Y and r0-r15. A 32-bit value spans two registers: the low word in the first.
- On success carry is clear. On error carry is set and A holds the error number.
- A call changes A, X, Y and the flags. It keeps r0-r15, except the registers it lists as out.
- A path is a pointer to a length-prefixed string.
- A handle goes in X, in and out.
- A drive number is 0 for A:, 1 for B:, and so on, except where a call says 0 is the current drive.

## What each call does

- `create`: Creates a file, or empties it if it exists, and opens it for reading and writing. The attributes take read only, hidden, system and archive. A directory, a read-only file, or a full drive gives error 5. A device name opens the device.
- `open`: Opens a file or a device. Access 1 or 2 on a read-only file gives error 5.
- `close`: Closes a handle. The directory entry of a file written through it takes the file's size and the archive bit.
- `read`: Reads bytes from a handle into memory.
- `write`: Writes bytes from memory to a handle. A write past the end of a file makes it longer. On a full drive r1 is less than the count.
- `seek`: Moves the position of a handle. A position may pass the end of the file; a read there gives 0 bytes. A device stays at 0.
- `delete`: Deletes a file. A read-only file gives error 5, a directory error 2. The kernel does not check for open handles: close the file first.
- `rename`: Renames a file or a directory, or moves a file to another directory on the same drive. A new name that exists, or a directory moved to another directory, gives error 5. The kernel does not check for open handles: close the file first.
- `attrib`: Gets or sets the attributes of a file.
- `filetime`: Gets or sets the time and date of an open file.
- `ioctl`: The subfunctions are those of MS-DOS 2.0 function 44h. Two are written. Subfunction 0, device info: r0 = the driver's DEV_ bits for a device, 0 for a file. `CON` gives $83, `NUL` $84. Subfunction 6, input status: r0 = $FF when a read would give a byte, else 0. A file gives 0 at or past its end. A device asks its driver: `CON` gives $FF when a key waits, `NUL` gives 0. Any other subfunction gives error 1.
- `dup`: Gives the first closed handle to the file of a handle. Both handles share the position.
- `dup2`: Makes a second handle refer to the file of the first, and closes the second first if it is open. Both handles share the position. A second handle equal to the first does nothing.
- `findfirst`: Finds the first name that matches a pattern with `*` and `?`. `*` matches any run of characters, dots too, and `?` matches one character. A pattern that ends in `.` or `.*` also matches a name with no dot. A pattern that ends in a separator matches every name in that directory. The pattern is up to 32 characters. Normal files always match; directories, hidden files and system files match only when their attribute bit is set in A. The volume label never matches.
- `findnext`: Finds the next name that matches the pattern of a find buffer.
- `mkdir`: Makes a directory. A name that exists, or a full drive, gives error 5.
- `str_alloc`: Takes a block of A bytes in the program's string heap and points the descriptor at r0 to its length byte. The text follows the length byte. A descriptor is 2 bytes in program RAM, or at $A000-$BFFF in the heap's bank. A full heap is compacted first. Compaction moves strings and rewrites their descriptors: read a descriptor again after any str_alloc or str_gc. The block of the descriptor's old string becomes free.
- `rmdir`: Removes an empty directory. A directory that holds entries other than . and .. gives error 5, the current directory of its drive error 16.
- `chdir`: Sets the current directory of a drive.
- `getcwd`: Gives the current directory of a drive, without the drive letter and the first \.
- `getdrive`: Gives the current drive.
- `setdrive`: Sets the current drive.
- `diskfree`: Gives the size and free space of a drive. The free clusters are the count in the FS info sector.
- `con_line`: Reads a line from the console with editing. Byte 0 of the buffer holds the most characters it takes, CR included, from 1 to 254. The call puts the length read, CR not included, in byte 1 and the text after it, ended by CR. Tab does nothing.
- `con_status`: Tells whether a key is waiting, and which modifier keys are held. `lib/KEYS.UXI` names the modifier bits.
- `exec`: Runs a program and returns when it ends. `exitcode` gives its code. The file starts with its load address, which must be $0801, and the rest loads at $0801. A program that starts with a BASIC line `SYS n` starts at n, any other at $0801. The program gets the command tail in its PSP at $0780: cut to 126 characters, and followed by a CR that the length does not count. Its handles are copies of the caller's. `exec` saves the caller's pages from $0700 to the page in its `PSP_TOP`, $0702, then its zero page from r0 to $7F, in RAM banks 1 to 10, right after the save of the program that ran the caller. A save that does not fit gives error 8, and so does a fifth program inside 4.
- `exit`: Ends the program and returns to its parent. `RTS` from the program's start is `exit` with code 0. Does not return, except with error 1 when no program is running.
- `exitcode`: Gives the exit code of the last program that ended.
- `keep`: Ends the program and keeps its RAM banks and its IRQ hook. Does not return.
- `bank_alloc`: Hands out a run of 8 KB RAM banks that follow each other: the lowest run that is free. A size of 0 gives the number of free banks and hands out nothing. The banks belong to the running program, and `exit` frees them. Error 8 when no run of the size is free.
- `bank_free`: Frees a run of banks from `bank_alloc`. Error 9 when A is not the first bank of a run of the running program.
- `getvect`: Gives a handler address.
- `setvect`: Sets a handler address.
- `getdate`: Gives the date from the RTC. The day of the week is worked out from the date.
- `setdate`: Sets the date of the RTC. A date that does not exist gives error 13. It also sets the RTC's weekday and its battery backup bit, VBATEN.
- `gettime`: Gives the time from the RTC.
- `settime`: Sets the time of the RTC, and starts its oscillator.
- `version`: Gives the system version.
- `ticks`: Gives the number of VSYNCs since boot.
- `errmsg`: Gives the message of an error number.
- `con_out`: Writes a character to the screen. A handle redirected does not take it. It obeys CR, LF, BS, TAB, BEL and FF, skips $0F, and obeys these escape sequences of MS-DOS's ANSI.SYS: `Esc[r;cH` moves the cursor to row r, column c; `Esc[2J` clears the screen and puts the cursor home; `Esc[K` blanks from the cursor to the end of the line; `Esc[...m` takes 0 for the color `con_colour` last set, 7 to swap the foreground and the background, 30 to 37 for the foreground and 40 to 47 for the background. Rows and columns count from 1. A missing parameter is 0, and 0 means 1 in `Esc[r;cH`. A row or column past the edge means the last. A sequence takes up to 4 parameters, each modulo 256. Other sequences do nothing. Esc then a byte other than `[` shows that byte. `lib/CONS.UXI` names the sequences.
- `con_in`: Waits for a key, without echo. An extended key gives two characters: 0, then its IBM PC BIOS scan code. The scan codes: Up $48, Down $50, Left $4B, Right $4D, Home $47, End $4F, PgUp $49, PgDn $51, Insert $52, Delete $53, F1 to F10 $3B to $44, with Shift $54 to $5D, with Ctrl $5E to $67, with Alt $68 to $71. Alt wins over Ctrl, and Ctrl over Shift. Ctrl+Left $73, Ctrl+Right $74, Ctrl+End $75, Ctrl+PgDn $76, Ctrl+Home $77, Ctrl+PgUp $84. Alt+1 to Alt+0, Alt+- and Alt+= $78 to $83. Alt with a letter gives the letter's scan code. Ctrl+2 gives 0, then 3. Ctrl with a letter, `[`, `\` or `]` gives $01 to $1D, Ctrl+6 $1E, Ctrl+- $1F. Ctrl with Space or with a key that gives a control character gives that character. Ctrl with any other key gives nothing, and so does Alt with a key other than a letter, a digit, - or =. `lib/KEYS.UXI` names every code.
- `con_cursor`: Gets the cursor's row and column with carry set, moves the cursor with carry clear. The screen has 30 rows and 80 columns.
- `str_free`: Frees the string of the descriptor at r0 and sets the descriptor to 0. A descriptor of 0 does nothing.
- `str_gc`: Compacts the program's string heap.
- `str_heap`: Chooses the program's string heap. Bank 11 is the shared heap, every program's at its start. A higher bank becomes a new, empty heap whose blocks start at r0; the bytes from $A00C to r0 are the program's.
- `con_colour`: Gets the console color with carry set, sets it with carry clear. The high nibble is the background and the low nibble the foreground, from VERA's palette. A new color takes effect for the characters written after the call.
- `con_break`: Gets the break mode and the break flag with carry set, sets the mode with carry clear. The mode says what Ctrl+C from the console does: 0 nothing, it is the character $03; 1 prints ^C and ends the program with exit code 0, and `exitcode` then gives X = 1; 2 drops the key and sets the flag. A get clears the flag. `exec` starts each program in mode 1. The console sees Ctrl+C only while a program asks it for a key.
- `con_getkey`: Reads a key in one call, extended or not, with carry clear waiting for it with the cursor blinking, with carry set returning at once. A plain key gives its character in A and 0 in X. An extended key gives 0 in A and its scan code in X, the codes of `con_in`. No key gives 0 in both. Y gives the modifiers, as `con_status` gives them in X.
- `con_edit`: Edits a line from the console, as `con_line` reads one, from the text in the buffer: byte 1 holds its length, 0 for none, and the text follows it. The call shows the text first. Enter, Tab or an extended key ends the line. Tab and the extended key are not echoed, and leave the cursor after the text. The registers come back as `con_getkey` gives them.
- `con_screen`: Reads a line from the console with the full-screen editor, into a buffer as `con_line` fills it. The cursor moves over the whole screen, and Enter returns the text of the cursor's row without the blanks at its end: from the column the call started at on the row it started at, from column 0 on any other row. A line is one row. The keys: the arrows; Ctrl+Left and Ctrl+Right a word; Home the top left corner; End after the row's text; Ctrl+Home clears the screen; Ctrl+End blanks to the end of the row; Esc blanks the row; Ins turns insert mode on or off, and a cursor move turns it off; Del and Backspace delete; Tab moves to the next column of 8, and in insert mode opens blanks. A Ctrl+C in break mode 2 ends the line with no text. When handle 0 is a file, the call is `con_line`.

## Find buffer

| Offset | Size | Field |
|---|---|---|
| 0 | 41 | the search, for findnext |
| 41 | 1 | attributes |
| 42 | 2 | time |
| 44 | 2 | date |
| 46 | 4 | size |
| 50 | 33 | name: a length byte, then up to 32 characters |
